items.title: How to Evaluate AI Chip Stocks: A Practical Framework
items.snippet:
## What Counts as an AI Chip Stock

An AI chip stock is a company whose value is...
items.raw_snippet:
## What Counts as an AI Chip Stock

An AI chip stock is a company whose value is closely tied to the silicon that powers artificial-intelligence workloads. That covers more ground than most people assume, and the sub-groups behave differently. [...] No single metric decides the case. What you are building is a composite read across everything above.

A strong-profile AI chip company tends to combine durable data-center revenue growth, high and stable gross margins, productive R&D intensity, defensible design wins, manageable foundry and customer concentration, and a valuation lens matched to its growth stage. A weakness in one area is not automatically disqualifying, but it should be understood and weighed against the others. [...] Concentration in one hot segment is both the opportunity and the risk. NVIDIA, for example, transformed over several years from a business defined by gaming graphics into one dominated by data-center revenue. That shift powered enormous growth, but it also means a large slice of the company now rides on a single end market. When that demand cools, the same concentration works in reverse. Reading the segment mix tells you how exposed a company is to the AI cycle, for better and worse.
